title: How to practice DSA so it actually sticks
author: Nishant Verma

pages.label: the trap
title: MORE PROBLEMS
IS NOT THE FIX
body: You can solve 400 problems and still
freeze on a variation you have not seen.
It is reasoning, out loud, under pressure.

pages.label: step 1  ·  start dumb
title: STATE THE
BRUTE FORCE
body: Too slow for n = 10 to the 5."

pages.label: step 2  ·  the real work
title: FIND THE
BOTTLENECK
pages.takeaway: The bottleneck tells you the tool.

pages.label: step 3  ·  the toolbox
title: PICK THE TOOL
body: hash map   - remember what you saw
heap       - keep the top k cheaply

pages.label: step 4  ·  the habit
title: EXPLAIN BEFORE
YOU CODE
body: Say the approach in plain words.
If you cannot explain it, you do not
own it yet. You are hoping.
pages.takeaway: The interviewer only hears your reasoning.

pages.label: step 5  ·  review right
title: TRACK WHY
IT WAS HARD
body: Not just that you solved it.
Write one line: what beat you,
Revisit the ones that beat you,
not the ones you already know.
pages.takeaway: Review the failures, not the wins.

pages.label: step 7  ·  depth
title: DO FEWER,
DEEPER
body: beat ten skimmed for the solution.
what class of problem is this?

pages.label: the test  ·  what it measures
title: WHAT IT
ACTUALLY TESTS
body: Interviews do not test whether you
They test whether you can reason
pages.takeaway: Reasoning is the skill. Practise that.

pages.label: start here  ·  today
title: TODAY'S ONE
CHANGE
body: Pick the last problem that beat you.
Re-solve it out loud, from scratch,
That single rep is worth more
pages.takeaway: Say it before you code it.
